investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T05:20–05:27Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint at the infrastructure layer, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod is never scheduled, and the probe times out without writing any required evidence fields.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 kata/peerpods nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful, ruling out priority-based recovery.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peerpods nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were removed, cordoned, or relabeled, the effective schedulable pool would drop to zero even without resource exhaustion.

Tertiary — cluster-level ResourceQuota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm set too low for concurrent eval probes: if multiple probe runs or production workloads share the same quota, concurrent demand could transiently exhaust the resource even if steady-state capacity is sufficient.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector in the pod spec is misconfigured or overly restrictive, causing more nodes than expected to be excluded; however, the message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' as the reason for the 2 eligible nodes, making a selector-only misconfiguration less likely as the sole cause.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T05:20–05:27Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the VM provisioning step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint at the infrastructure layer, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod is never scheduled, and the probe times out without writing any required evidence fields.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 kata/peerpods nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful, ruling out priority-based recovery.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peerpods nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were removed, cordoned, or relabeled, the effective schedulable pool would drop to zero even without resource exhaustion.

Tertiary — cluster-level ResourceQuota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm set too low for concurrent eval probes: if multiple probe runs or production workloads share the same quota, concurrent demand could transiently exhaust the resource even if steady-state capacity is sufficient.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector in the pod spec is misconfigured or overly restrictive, causing more nodes than expected to be excluded; however, the message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' as the reason for the 2 eligible nodes, making a selector-only misconfiguration less likely as the sole cause.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T05:25–05:27Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a running agent, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: the scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that the two VM-capable nodes are fully allocated and no preemption victims exist. The eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 seconds before the check timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a complete contract violation. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two VM-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pods. Preemption is also unavailable ('No preemption victims found'), so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even checked.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or production workload may have consumed the remaining VM slots and not yet released them, leaving the cluster in a saturated state at the time of this eval run. No history data is available (previousRunCount=0) to confirm whether this is a new regression or a recurring saturation event.

Lower probability — a misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more than 1 VM unit per pod) could cause exhaustion faster than expected, but the scheduler message does not indicate an oversized request.
